original.reason: The key lemma is false: from representability of 0,...,C_n-1 one cannot infer that C_n+1,...,C_n+M_n are representable, since this would require all corresponding sums up to M_n to already lie in S_n. Thus completeness need not arise after one added term.

judgment.reason: It incorrectly asserts that adding c_n yields every sum c_n through c_n+M_n. Only c_n+t for t in T_n is obtained, and T_n need not contain that whole interval.
Its central lemma is false: minimality of c_n supplies only 0,...,c_n-1 in T_n, not all 0,...,M_n needed for the asserted shifted interval.
The claimed transition from a first gap to complete subset-sum coverage is unsupported and false in general; the displayed shifted interval assumes T_k contains all values through M_k.

The ‘standard first-gap argument applied successively’ does not establish representability of x-c_n for arbitrary values through M_n. This is the same false completeness lemma, merely stated less precisely.
